content.text:
Checking out a reference item (`reference: true`) is now refused with `{ ok: false, reason: 'not-lendable' }`. The full suite passes (60 tests), including a new one for this case.

I put the rule in `isLendable` in `lib/catalog/items.js`. It now also requires `item.reference !== true`, and I updated its doc comment. `checkOutItem` already refuses non-lendable items with `'not-lendable'`, so it needed no change, and `isLendable` has no other callers.

The new test in `test/checkout.test.js` checks an in-service reference item. It is refused with `'not-lendable'` and no loan is created.

Your message also says the desk "can still check them out". I read that as the desk can still try the checkout and gets a refusal, since the refusal reason contradicts the other reading. If you meant something else, such as a librarian override, tell me.

I didn't add a `reference` field to the sample data. The test builds its reference item inline.
